findings.issue_category: hardcoded cloud credentials in environment variables
findings.description: The Lambda function embeds a static AWS access key ID and secret access key directly in its environment variables. These plaintext credentials are stored in the Terraform state/config and are readable by anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, allowing credential theft and unauthorized AWS access.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption at rest for env vars
findings.description: No kms_key_arn is specified, so Lambda environment variables (which here contain secrets) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key rather than a customer-managed CMK, providing no separate key-policy access control over the secret material.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unpatched.
No code_signing_config_arn is configured, so Lambda does not verify that the deployment package is signed by a trusted publisher, permitting deployment of tampered or malicious code.

The function has no vpc_config block, so it runs outside any VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security-group/network ACL controls, which increases exfiltration risk for a function holding credentials.
